built: canonical/runtime/appearance_address_v1.py -- resolves a goal against a candidate set using the modality the goal implies: COLOUR (computed background), TEXT (text/aria/title/alt), GLYPH (single-character targets). Refuses with a named status rather than guessing.
design_basis: 2026 hybrid-consensus: accessibility tree first, rendered-appearance fallback. zylos 2026: accessibility-only 73.1% vs hybrid 89.1% on WebVoyager. 'Use the accessibility tree when it exists, fall back to Set-of-Marks where the tree is empty.'

measurement.what_changed: the failure list changed completely, which is the informative part

per_task.why: the anchor was addressable through a modality the text-only channel missed

MiniWob renders duplicate swatches; nearest-colour has genuine ties. The module refuses instead of picking one and silently being wrong 50% of the time. A refusal is progress when the alternative is a coin flip.
the glyph x is not exposed as a visible candidate element by the harvest query (it is a styled div with a background, not text and not an accessible character)
clicking the top-level menu item does not open the submenu under a synthetic mouse event in this build
the goal 'Click the button' contains no addressable token at all
the options do not exist in the DOM until the select is opened; enumerating them requires an open-then-read step

honest_conclusion: the appearance channel fixed one task and converted one silent error into a correct refusal. It did not move the score. The remaining four failures are NOT perception-modality problems: they are (a) a target with no addressable token, (b) a collapsed widget that must be opened before it can be enumerated, (c) a submenu that does not open, (d) a glyph that is drawn rather than exposed.
correction_to_my_own_r123_claim: I said 'the fix is to look at it'. I built the looking, and it was worth exactly one task. The coefficient is not raised by adding one more reading modality; two of the four remaining blockers need INTERACTION (open the select, open the submenu) rather than better perception.
the_more_precise_limiting_factor: among the four remaining failures, two require the agent to open a closed widget and then re-read the world -- an interact-then-observe loop -- and two involve targets with no addressable token or glyph at all. Neither is solved by a better static reader, and neither is solved by a better learner.
what_this_means_for_the_users_thesis: instant learning multiplies whatever the agent can perceive AND OPERATE. Opening a collapsed widget is an operation, not a perception. The remaining gap is operational, which is consistent with the component-benchmark finding that action-space coverage (not learning) bounds end-to-end reliability.
